title: Choose the visual world for Beams & Braces
question: The roll assigned The Construction Poster. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Construction Poster
options.lineage: Swiss International Typographic Style, 1950s–60s construction and exhibition posters
options.thesis: The site as an objective Swiss poster: real photographs, a strict grid, and facts set as typographic events.
materials: a grid built on the 140mm board
options.viewport: The aerial plan shot fills seven columns and bleeds off the edge. The headline hangs flush-left, the credentials stack below it, and a solid Ocracoke-rust Let's Chat bar sits on the baseline.
options.risk: Swiss rigour can tip into cold or corporate if the photography and Darren's voice aren't given the room.

raised.raise: All 13 colours stand as one continuous bench of identical board specimens at the same scale, read by sweeping the row, never one card at a time.
Two-ink discipline: charcoal and one rust signal only. Credentials are stacked by rank, like a bill's line-up.
The layout only ever repeats in whole modules: the grid unit is one board width plus its gap, never a fraction.
No cards and no boxes: content rides baselines on one unit, and rules exist only where a board edge would.
Text always sits on the nearest plane. Photographs are never tinted or overlaid with type.
Swatch states read beyond colour: selected shows name, range and warranty in type, not just a ring.

options.label: The Setting-Out Drawing
options.thesis: Every page as Darren's setting-out drawing: plan views, radii and dimension strings drawn over real work.
options.viewport: The aerial deck plan with its curve radius, board run and joist spacing called out in fine linework.
options.risk: Blueprint styling is a familiar move, and linework can read as decoration if the numbers aren't real.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Identical instruments shoulder to shoulder, read by sweeping the row.
options.viewport: A row of board meters leaning together.
options.case: Homeowners don't identify with studio gear, and needles don't clarify decking.
options.risk: Pure metaphor with no product truth to measure.
options.kept: The 13 colours as one sweepable bench of identical specimens.

options.label: Zoot Dance-Hall Handbill
options.thesis: Billing order is the hierarchy, printed in two heavy inks.
options.viewport: Credentials stacked as a bill line-up.
options.case: Nostalgic costume that fights the premium, waterside audience.
options.kept: Two-ink discipline and credentials stacked by rank.

options.label: Pastel Character Sheet
options.thesis: A sweet mascot sheet with a repeating motif border.
options.case: No identification for the audience and no clarity about decking.
options.kept: Repetition in whole units only: the board module.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.thesis: One bitmap face on a black void, where rank is depth.
options.viewport: A single ivory line over drifting grey dust.
options.case: Night-time hacker culture is the opposite of a Broads garden.
options.kept: No boxes or dividers; everything rides baselines.

options.label: Multiplane Cel Dawn
options.thesis: Painted planes sliding at different speeds toward a lit cottage.
options.case: Painting replaces the real photographs this site must show.
options.kept: Text on the nearest plane; photos never tinted.

options.label: Silk Canopy Chords
options.thesis: Translucent silk bands overlapping into colour chords.
options.case: Abstract colour play obscures real board colours, where accuracy is the point.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The premium decking site everyone ships: dark photo hero, serif headline, gold CTA, badge strip, range cards, review carousel.
canonCard.viewport: A darkened hero photo with a centred serif headline and two buttons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition, and close to the current site.
